newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sweden reveals funding to S.Africa opposition.
newsitem.headline: Sweden reveals funding to S.Africa opposition.

text.p: Swedish Foreign Affairs Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen on Thursday disclosed the extent of Sweden's support for the anti-apartheid struggle, saying it had spent about $400 million to help bring down white minority rule.

A team of Swedish investigators is in South Africa to look into allegations by former security branch officers that colleagues of theirs were behind the still unsolved murder of Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme in 1986.
Hjelm-Wallen, on her first visit to South Africa, told a news conference that the extent of the funding was kept secret even from Swedes.
"We have for so many years been so close to South Africans in their struggle against apartheid," she said.
"You can also count it in terms of what we have disbursed to South Africans for the period in which the struggle took place, and that is about $400 million.
"This is a very big sum and in Sweden it was secret -- we couldn't tell even the Swedish public about it. But now we can publicly tell how it was," Hjelm-Wallen said.
Sweden was a staunch campaigner for an all-race democratic dispensation in South Africa, and has since signed numerous aid agreements with post-apartheid South Africa.
